345989.title: The pagenumber conjecture for complete expansion graphs
345989.statement:

$$
pn(\mathcal{E}_{c}(K_n))=\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil.

346024.title: The inverse-exponent conjecture for direct factors of cyclic groups
346024.statement:
Let $k$, $\omega$, and $n$ be positive integers, and let $\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$ be a finite cyclic group of order $\omega$. Suppose

$$
A=[0,n-k-1]\cup\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\omega},\qquad |A|=n\geq 2k+1.
$$

A subset $A$ is a **direct factor** of $\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$ if it occurs as one factor in a direct factorization of that cyclic group. **Inverse-exponent conjecture.** If $A$ is a direct factor of $\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$, then

$$
\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\equiv\{n-k,n-k+1,\ldots,n-1\}\pmod n.
$$

The conjecture is the cyclic-group factorization counterpart of the multiplier-set conjecture above; the source notes that the corresponding assertion is known for $k\leq 2$, while the general case remains open.

346148.title: Shareshian's wedge-of-spheres conjecture for subgroup intervals
346148.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $H<G$. Define the open subgroup interval

$$
\widehat{\mathcal{L}(H,G)}=\{K\mid H<K<G\}.
$$

**Shareshian's conjecture.** The order complex of $\widehat{\mathcal{L}(H,G)}$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.
This conjecture predicts a spherical wedge structure for the order complexes of all open intervals in subgroup lattices. The paper's result that the relevant order complex is contractible for $G\cong PGL_2(p^{2^n})$, with $p$ odd and $n\geq1$, is consistent with the conjecture, since a contractible complex can be regarded as a wedge of zero spheres.

346193.title: The rainbow matching conjecture for general graphs
346193.statement:
Let $(m,n)\to k$ mean that every $m$ matchings of size $n$ in any graph have a rainbow matching of size $k$. The notation $(m,n)\to_{\mathcal{B}} k$ has the same meaning for bipartite graphs. **Rainbow matching conjecture.**

$$
(2n,n)\to n.
$$

If $n$ is odd, then

$$
(2n-1,n)\to n.
$$

The bipartite analogue $(2n-1,n)\to_{\mathcal{B}}n$ is known by Drisko's theorem. The conjecture asserts that passing from bipartite graphs to general graphs costs only one additional matching; it remains open in the supplied source.

346567.title: The 1/3–2/3 Conjecture for finite posets
346567.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset on $n$ elements. A linear extension is an order-preserving bijection $bb:P\to[n]$, and for $x,y\in P$ define

$$
\delta_P(x,y)=\frac{|\{\text{linear extensions }\lambda:P\to[n]\text{ such that }\lambda(x)>\lambda(y)\}|}{|\{\text{linear extensions of }P\}|}.
$$

The **balance constant** of $P$ is

$$
b(P)=\max_{x,y\in P}\min(\delta_P(x,y),1-\delta_P(x,y)).
$$

**The 1/3–2/3 Conjecture.** For any finite poset $P$ which is not a total order, $b(P)\geq\frac{1}{3}$.

This is a longstanding open problem in the theory of posets, with the bound proved for several special classes, including width-two posets. The conjecture asks for a universal information-theoretic lower bound on how balanced some pair of incomparable elements must be.

346735.title: Finiteness conjecture for irreducible solutions of $(E_N)$
346735.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}^{*}$ with $N\geq 2$. A solution of $(E_N)$ is called **irreducible** when it cannot be decomposed as a sum of two nontrivial solutions, as in the preceding discussion. **Finiteness conjecture.** The equation $(E_N)$ has only finitely many irreducible solutions.

This is the first of two conjectures motivated by the cases treated in the paper. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

346857.title: Constant-solution conjecture for positive-edge-length tEoM settings on $T_q$
346857.statement: Let $T_q$ be the graph under consideration, let $M_q$ be a setting of its edge lengths, and let the tEoM denote the discrete time equations of motion. Assume that all edge lengths in $M_q$ are positive and that there is a vertex $i\in T_q$ at which all connected edges have equal lengths. The **constant-solution conjecture** states that if $M_q$ solves the tEoM, then $M_q$ is a constant solution. The conjecture concerns existence and persistence of positive solutions; the paper motivates it by observing that evolution away from an equal-edge vertex should otherwise produce nonpositive edge lengths after finitely many steps.
